(p-44) **Sūrat al-Jumu'ah (Surah al-Jumu'ah)**

Its central purpose is to explain the named subject of *al-Ṣaff* (the ranks), through a proof that is the clearest of the religion's laws and the most secure of Islam's bonds. This is the Friday congregational prayer (*al-Jumu'ah*), whose name indicates the purpose for which it exists: the obligation to gather for it and the requirement to attend it, which means setting aside everything else and devoting oneself to what was neglected through dispersal during the sermon. Those who were sent for purification (*tazkiyah*) gather together for it, as they do in jihad and other matters, in hardship and ease, in what is desired and what is disliked. Its name, *al-Jumu'ah*, is the most suitable thing about it for this purpose, through reflection on its verses and contemplation of their beginnings and ends. These verses urge strong mutual connection and union, and lead to the constant turning toward the One who purifies, along with love for Him and following Him.

*Bismillah* (In the name of God), whose knowledge encompasses every object of knowledge, so His explanation is complete. *Al-Raḥmān* (the Most Merciful), whose blessing of explanation is general, following the universal honor of His act of bringing into existence; He is therefore great in His dignity. *Al-Raḥīm* (the Most Compassionate), who singled out His party for success in what pleases Him, so that each of them is firmly established in their love for Him and their faith in Him.

* *

When the preceding surah, *al-Ṣaff*, ended with the turning of some of the Children of Israel toward His Most Holy Presence after they had deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate, all of them or the deviant among them, as the use of the pronoun over them implies. Then He strengthened those among them who persisted in deviation. Thus it is established that He has complete power, which necessarily entails comprehensive knowledge, and from which follows His transcendence above every trace of deficiency. He, glory be to Him, had mentioned glorification (*tasbīḥ*), which is the greatest and most well-known form of declaring Him free from imperfection (*tanzīh*), in the past tense three times at the openings of three surahs. That is the highest degree of emphatic affirmation. Thus it is established that His transcendence has been proclaimed by every speaker and every silent thing. At the beginning of this surah He informed us that this declaration of transcendence occurs in a renewed and continuous manner, by using the present tense to indicate the continuity of His dominion. So He said: ﴿Glorifies﴾, that is, brings about the greatest, most splendid, and most perfect declaration of transcendence, ﴿God﴾, that is, the King who encompasses everything in power and knowledge. He emphasized this because of what is in *al-Taghābun* (the mutual deception). Having affirmed that it occurs in this manner, He did not need to repeat the emphasis more than once. He placed between each pair of glorifying surahs a surah free of such language, so that this would indicate more clearly the intention of emphasis, by the intensity of attention given to the remembrance, even though a separation occurred. The emphasis becomes more alerting and more effective in awakening and reminding.

Since rebuking the rational speaker for failing to obey is more severe than rebuking the silent, He said: ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾. Although the rational being is included in this, so that his glorification is sometimes voluntary, in agreement with the command, and sometimes unwilling, through submission accompanied by his own will, the glorification of the silent is always voluntary. Since the address was to those who believed, that called for emphasis because they needed it, so He said: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, likewise.

Since the three preceding surahs established that existent things have brought about glorification of Him, and this surah informed us that this continues in a renewed manner, that indicates, together with the declaration of transcendence from deficiencies, the affirmation of perfection, which belongs only to a king of great dignity whose command is obeyed. Because restricting the statement to the silent by using a word that is apparent in them might have given rise to some misunderstanding, He stated explicitly what the context implied: ﴿the King﴾, that is, the one to whom all perfections belong. He gives victory to whomever He wills among His soldiers, even if they were humiliated, so they become manifest. ﴿The Holy (al-Quddūs)﴾, from whom all deficiencies are negated, so nothing exists except by His permission. He is exalted above any creature's encompassing of His knowledge or grasping the reality of His essence. Thus creatures have nothing in their hands except to contemplate the witnessing of His actions and to reflect upon the meanings of His attributes and majesty. The most deserving of them of nearness and inclusion in His party is the one who takes on His attributes according to the degree of his striving. It is therefore incumbent upon the believer to avoid saying what he does not do, or building any of his affairs on something lacking firm foundation. The explanation of these two noble names has already passed shortly before, and He mentioned the essence of their explanation through what is the distinctive attribute of sovereignty and the sign of purity for the pure: ﴿the Mighty (al-ʿAzīz)﴾, that is, the One who overcomes everything, and nothing overcomes Him. Had He willed, He would have made all rational beings, along with their glorification through submission to His purpose, both willingly and unwillingly, glorifying Him by agreeing to His command willingly. ﴿The Wise (al-Ḥakīm)﴾, who brings about everything He wills in its most fitting, most complete, and most perfect place.

Abū Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When the surah of *al-Ṣaff* ended with praise of the disciples (*al-Ḥawāriyyūn*) for the excellence of their response and the beauty of their faith, and He had commanded the believers to imitate them in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of God, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my helpers for God?"﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14], and so on, this might give the impression that the followers of Jesus, peace be upon him, are superior to the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ). So this surah follows that with a mention of this community and praise of it. The surah opens with a declaration of transcendence from what was alluded to in His saying: ﴿but a group disbelieved﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14], for they committed a great sin and claimed prophethood. So He, glory be to Him, declared Himself free of that. Then He said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered (*al-Ummiyyīn*) a messenger from among themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], up to His saying: ﴿and God is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 4]. Then, exalted is He, informed us about the condition of a group upon whom the light of guidance shone and for whom the path of truth became clear, but who became blind to that, were bewildered in the darkness of their ignorance, and did not increase, by what they carried, except in confusion and misguidance. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the example of a donkey carrying books﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 5], and the verses that follow. These verses are in the context of warning those who were previously praised and granted God's mercy, so that they would not be, in what their Prophet recites to them of the signs and teaches them of the Book and wisdom, like those tested ones. For those were despised and cursed after carrying the Torah, though they claimed that they had undertaken to carry it and fulfill it. So He admonished these by their example, as an act of kindness from God to this community. And none remember except the people of understanding. End.

The Ummiyyun (the unlettered, those without a book) are the Arabs, who were known among the nations for not writing; they remained in their original state from the time they came out of their mothers' wombs. The mention of the time of the sending and the omission of its end indicate that it extends to everyone to whom the sending can reach, which is all of creation. It is also permissible to apply the term "unlettered" to all the people of the earth, because his (ﷺ) sending came when knowledge had departed from people, and because the Arabs are the root, so all the others are followers of them. There is no strangeness in his being sent to them with their description, ﴿a messenger﴾. And since rectifying a thing by its own kind is more wondrous, He said: ﴿from among them﴾. Rather, "unlettered" [in the sense of] not writing and being free of every artificial quality, a quality that is constantly necessary for him, and his knowing what he did not know without seeking it. So the traces of humanness were effaced in him, and the lights of realities shone upon him. This might lead one to imagine that he needed to seek help from books. The origin of his resemblance to the condition of those among whom he was sent is closer to their equality with him, were it possible for them; so the impossibility of equality is a stronger proof of the miraculous nature (of his message). And mentioning [his being sent] from among them, if the description is restricted to the Arabs, does not negate his being sent to others, especially with what has been reported about it in explicit texts and the decisive proofs he established. So He mentioned the place and starting point of the sending, and the end is thereby unrestricted, its implied meaning being: to all of creation.

Since his being from among them would imply that he is no more exalted than them, or only slightly so, He marvelled at his affair and drew attention to a great miracle of his by saying, in a new sentence: ﴿He recites﴾, that is, He reads a recitation whose parts follow one another in abundance, elevation and loftiness, ﴿to them﴾, despite his being unlettered like them, ﴿His signs﴾, that is, He brings them to them continuously and in succession, a clear sign of his truthfulness, because he is unlettered like them. Rather, among them are writers and scholars, and although they are numerous, [yet] He did not single him out from them with this except the One who is capable of all things.

Since the station calls for purification [and for disciplining those who fell into befriending the disbelievers and the like], He put purification first, saying: ﴿and purifies them﴾, that is, from base morals and deviant beliefs. His purification of them during his lifetime was by his noble gaze upon them, his teaching them, and his reciting to them. Sometimes he looked at a person with a look of love, and Allah purified him through it. Sometimes that look spread to a second person, and its lights shone upon him according to his capacities, as happened to Umayr ibn Wahb, then Safwan ibn Umayya, and likewise Dhu'l-Nur al-Tufayl ibn 'Amr al-Dawsi (may Allah be pleased with him), then He set him straight. As for Umayr, he was among the greatest harmers of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of those who believed in him. He discussed with Safwan, at al-Hijr, the Battle of Badr and those of their chieftains whom they had lost, and that there was no good in life after them. Then they wished for a man to fight the Prophet (ﷺ). Umayr said: "Were it not for my poverty, and my daughters and dependants, whom I fear will be lost after me, I would go to him with the mule of my captive among them and kill him." Safwan seized the opportunity and pledged to provide for his dependants if he died, and to support him if he lived. He said: "Keep this secret from me for three days." Then he went to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah guided him. Safwan swore that he would never speak to him again. When Makkah was conquered, Safwan fled to board a ship from Jeddah. Umayr asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission, then went after him, caught up with him, and did not cease to persuade him until he returned. Then he embraced Islam and became one of the excellent Companions (may Allah be pleased with him). As for Dhu'l-Nur, when the Prophet (ﷺ) invited him, he asked for a sign by which Allah would help him against his people. So Allah gave him a light when he came to the clan to which he belonged. Then he invited his father and mother, and they both embraced Islam. Then he accompanied him in the same way, and then He set him straight, and none of them remained behind. As for others besides the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), his purification of them is through his traces, according to their capacities and the matters which Allah has decreed to be prepared. Whoever was more passionately devoted to him was more bound to follow him, and so he was more firmly rooted in the Book of Allah and His Sunnah than those of the (prophetic) biography and others in knowledge and practice, and so he was more purified.

Since they, after the purification, which is clearing away of vices, were most in need of adornment with virtues, He said: ﴿and teaches them the Book﴾, that is, the revealed book, which comprises every religious and worldly good in this world and the next, ﴿and the wisdom﴾. It is the ultimate purpose of the Book in the strength of understanding it and acting upon it. So it is knowledge adorned by action, and action perfected by knowledge, both what is rationally understood and what is transmitted, so that they may place every matter of it in its most fitting place, and thus not deviate from the Book as the Children of Israel deviated. Their likeness would then be the likeness of the donkey carrying books. Even if he (ﷺ) had no miracle except this, it would be sufficient as an ultimate [proof].

Since the description "unlettered" implies misguidance, and since many of them at the time this sura was revealed believed themselves to be upon a firm religion and a noble, clear condition, and since after his guiding them they would go astray (after being unlettered), because the sending from the presence of the unseen of the unseen [brings] knowledge contrary to being unlettered, to a degree no nation before them had attained, and since that would necessitate doubt about whether they had been unlettered, He emphasised this implication by saying: (p-52) ﴿Although they were﴾, that is, while in fact they were, a state that was innate to them. Since their being thus belongs to a past time, He introduced the preposition, saying: ﴿before﴾, that is, before his being sent to them, from the time they changed the religion of their father Isma'il (peace be upon him) and worshipped idols, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is, far from the intended goal, ﴿manifest﴾, that is, evident in itself, proclaiming to others that it is error, through their belief in obvious falsehoods, their supposition that they were upon something, the general ignorance that was theirs, their contentment with it, their choosing it, and their reproaching whoever inclined toward learning and sought insight, as happened to them with Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl and others. Describing them with this is an extreme negation of their having learned anything from any created being from their Prophet, to magnify what he brought of miraculous nature and to affirm how greatly they needed a prophet who would guide them to guidance and rescue them from the blindness and destruction in which they were.

﴿Wa-ākharīna﴾ ... ﴿And others﴾

Since His purifying them (the Arabs), despite their being unlettered (ummiyya) and dull-witted, was a remarkable matter in indicating complete power, given the attribute of being unlettered in ignorance, He increased that indication by joining to them many from other nations who are like them in being unlettered. So He said: ﴿And others﴾, meaning and He sent (him) to others ﴿among them﴾, in unlettered-ness and not in Arabness, ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾, meaning at any time in the past, in any attribute. Rather, they are the coarsest of people, such as the common folk of the Magians, Jews, Christians, Berbers and the like of the groups of the ʿAjam (non-Arabs), who are the most barbarous of people in speech, the most rigid in minds, and the most dense in nature and condition. God will join them with them in knowledge and purification.

Since their not being joined in the past might have suggested something about power, and their being joined in the future is the utmost indication of power, He said: ﴿And He is the al-ʿAzīz (the Almighty)﴾, meaning and the state being that He alone ﴿is the Almighty﴾, who is able over everything and whom nothing overcomes. So He purifies whom He wills and teaches him what He wishes, from whatever group he is, even if he were the most rigid of that group, because all things are in His hand. ﴿al-Ḥakīm (the All-Wise)﴾: so when He wills something that accords with His law and command, He makes it in the most perfect and firmest manner, so it cannot be undone. Whatever He wills, however it is, it must be carried out, so its rejection is never permitted in any way.

The intended meaning of "others" is the ʿAjam, and that God, may He be exalted, will join them with the Arabs. This is related from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, may Allah be pleased with him as well, and it is a narration of Layth from Mujāhid. It is supported by what is related from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man asked about them when Surah al-Jumuʿa (The Congregation) was revealed, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his hand on Salmān, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "If faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would reach it."

Since this was a dazzling matter, He magnified it by saying, in the manner of pointing to His power over it: ﴿That﴾, i.e., this matter of great rank, namely the preferring of the Messenger and his purifying of them and making them leaders after they had been followers, with no weight in the eyes of others among the nations. ﴿is the bounty of Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection; and bounty (fadl) is what is not owed, in contrast to an obligation (farḍ). ﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾, by His power and strength, by preparing it for him, even if he was the furthest of people from it. ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾ And since the word "āl" (possessor of, i.e., the definite article "al" with the emphatic form) indicates perfection, He pointed to that by saying: ﴿the Mighty﴾, i.e., the One before whom every other gift from anyone else is belittled.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 62, verse 5:

When He (exalted is He) had disciplined His believing servants in Surah al-Mumtahanah regarding what harms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and completed it in Surah al-Saff with what He warned of, namely the turning of hearts (izaghat al-qulub) against those who harmed His Prophet Musa (upon him be peace), and [since] I know that He (exalted is He) gathered all the manners (al-adab) in this Book which He revealed to their Prophet, whom He made the Seal of the Prophets and the most noble of the chosen ones, and He indicated His great favour by teaching the ignorant, He indicated His painful punishment, completing the indication of His manifest power by making the learned ignorant through the turning of his heart and the removal of his intellect, by his despair of the Hereafter, because of His anger against him, as a warning against falling into what necessitates misguidance after knowledge. So He said, as an answer to one who as if said: "This is His favour toward the ignorant, so what is His action toward the learned?" (p-55) He said, warning against one who purifies himself yet does not purify himself, by saying what he does not do, and who carries the Book yet carries it without knowing it, lest he be treated as the Jews were treated, with humiliation in this world and disgrace [and punishment] in the Hereafter, through the turning of hearts and the encompassing of sins, so that it becomes worse than what was said about it.

They said:
"Whoever misses knowledge and fails to attain wealth,
That one and the dog are equal in the same state."

﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ﴾ ("The likeness of those who"): Since knowledge, especially the divine (rabbani) kind, must be rejoiced in and desired from whatever source it comes, He used the passive form in His saying, and to protect His noble name from being mentioned in connection with disobedience: ﴿حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ﴾ ("were charged with the Torah"), meaning they were obligated and required to bear the Book which Allah gave to the Children of Israel through the tongue of Musa (upon him be peace), by His teaching it to them (exalted is He) and charging them to preserve its wording from alteration and forgetting, its meanings from distortion and confusion, and its limits and rulings from neglect and loss.

Since their abandoning of bearing it, though it is from Allah and through the tongue of a man from among them, is greater in their own estimation and more grave in terms of the kindness shown to them, especially with the long passage of time which facilitates its preservation, made easy for you to reflect upon and to recognize its worth, He expressed it with the particle of distance and said: ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها﴾ ("then they did not bear it"), in that they preserved its wording but did not act upon what is in it of the command to follow Isa (upon him be peace) when he came to them, and then Muhammad (ﷺ) when he came. So it harms them by its testimony against them, casting them into the Fire without any benefit at all. ﴿كَمَثَلِ﴾ ("like the likeness of") meaning: like the example of ﴿الحِمارِ﴾ ("the donkey"), which is the most foolish of animals, so it is an example [in] stupidity, while it ﴿يَحْمِلُ أسْفارًا﴾ ("carries books"), meaning books of knowledge that unveil matters and benefit the people of understanding. (Safar is the plural of sifr, which is the large book that reveals what is in it.)

Since the common example that unites both of them, which is the point of resemblance, is a person heavily burdened and exhausted by something from which he gains no benefit at all, so it is pure harm to him, and he does not perceive what he is carrying, except that he is wearied, and he does not know whether it is a rock or books, He produced His saying, expressing it with the particle which is for gathering censure, as a warning to human beings lest they be lax regarding any of the rulings of the Qur'an and thus become a worse example than the People of the Book, and fall below the donkey, because their Messenger (ﷺ) is greater and their Book is higher and more magnificent. So He said: ﴿بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القَوْمِ﴾ ("Evil is the example of the people"), meaning those who have strong power to attempt what they desire, yet are not granted any incapacity by which they may be excused, ﴿الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا﴾ ("who denied"), meaning they deliberately, with knowledge, persisted out of obstinacy and disbelief, ﴿بِآياتِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("the signs of Allah"), meaning the indications of the Supreme King upon His messengers, especially Muhammad (ﷺ), and all that pleases Him. Such people have indeed been described as sharing with the donkey in a quality which is the inner spirit, namely pure harm with no benefit in any way, while the most beneficial of things is that which points to Allah, which guarantees the happiness of both abodes. And although this example is explicitly about the Jews, it applies to all the readers of evil from every religious community, since they share with them in the point of resemblance, just as the example of the dog in al-A'raf is of this kind. It seems that He (exalted is He) did not explicitly include this Ummah in that, as an indication of its preservation without leaving it to itself, just as He gave it knowledge despite its being unlettered, from itself and from its Messenger, without leaving them to writing, nor to prior knowledge of any kind, nor to any burdensome effort.

Since the implied sense is: they deserved the description with all blameworthy traits, because they were wronged with the utmost wrong, His saying is joined to it: ﴿واللَّهُ﴾ ("And Allah"), meaning the One to whom belong all attributes of perfection, ﴿لا يَهْدِي القَوْمَ﴾ ("does not guide the people"), (this was the original form, but He made it more general and attached the judgment to the description) so He said: ﴿الظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("the wrongdoers"), meaning those who deliberately committed wrong by rejecting the guidance, which is the clear exposition that left no ambiguity, until wrongdoing became a firmly established trait for them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 62, verse 6:

Since their claim that they are the friends of Allah and His beloved was at the furthest extreme from this comparison, he proceeded with what proves the soundness of the comparison decisively. So he said, turning away from them and commanding (the Prophet) to rebuke those who denied him: ﴿Say﴾, that is, O Messenger, whom they are certain is the Messenger of Allah: ﴿O you who have become Jews﴾, that is, who have adopted Judaism. Since the truth splits open anyone who has the slightest sense (of right), and they were deserving of turning back from obstinacy, he used the particle of doubt and said: ﴿if you claim﴾, that is, you have said a statement that is open to denial, and for this reason you emphasized it, ﴿that you are friends of Allah﴾, that is, of the Supreme King, to whom no one has any command, (a friendship) He singled you out for with a special, original distinction ﴿apart from﴾, that is, the lowest in rank among the ranks of ﴿mankind﴾. So the friendship did not extend beyond that lowest rank to anyone other than you, but rather He singled you out from everyone who has the capacity for movement, especially the Gentiles (ummiyyun). ﴿Then wish for death﴾ and report about yourselves this, due to the fewness (of your time) in the abode of trial before reaching the place of honor and blessings. ﴿If you are﴾, that is, as a firm state, ﴿truthful﴾, that is, deeply rooted in your own estimation in truthfulness, for among the signs of love is longing for the beloved, and among the proofs of its sincerity is that whoever is in distress, and has a friend who has promised him, upon arrival at him, the comfort that is not mixed with harm, wishes to be transferred to his friend. It is narrated that he (ﷺ) said to them: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you will say it except that he chokes on his saliva." So none of them said it, knowing (in their hearts) the truthfulness of the one who confirmed it (ﷺ); they did not say it and did not believe, out of obstinacy.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 62, verse 7:

Since the implied meaning (taqdir, the sense supplied by the context) was: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them, in compliance with Our command, "Wish for death," so they did not wish for it at the present time, as confirmation from Us of his prophethood, as a challenge, and as a verification of the miracles of his mission (p. 59), this implied meaning is indicated by what is conjoined to it from His saying, which definitively indicates his truthfulness through their confirming him by refraining from what he reported they would not do: ﴿and they will never wish for it﴾, that is, in the future. He was content with this in the expression with "lā" (not), because what is mentioned of their claim here is that they are "allies of God," not "all the allies of God," so it falls short of a claim of exclusive right to the Hereafter. Also, wilāyah (guardianship, closeness) is for reaching Paradise, and exclusive enjoyment of the blessing does not necessarily follow from it, as evidenced by the fact that this world is not exclusively for the allies whose wilāyah is established, but the righteous and the wicked share in it. When He reported their not wishing for it, He widened the scope for them in order to establish the intended meaning, so He said: ﴿ever﴾. It is understood that its cause is their knowledge that they are "enemies of God," so He said: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾. Since most actions are done by the hand, He attributed all of them to it, because it has become an expression for power, so He said: ﴿their hands﴾, that is, of the sins that encompassed them, so they left them no share in the Hereafter, given their knowledge.

Since the implied meaning, as a consequence of this, was: lest they say, "We accept everything that has been said about the wrongdoers, but we are not of them," God, who is All-Knowing of them in their actions and intentions, conjoined to it His saying, attaching it to the attribute for generality and to inform that the description of what they had sent forward of wrongdoing: ﴿And God﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all-encompassing power and knowledge, ﴿is All-Knowing﴾, that is, of perfect knowledge, encompassing them. This was the original form, but He said: ﴿of the wrongdoers﴾ (p. 60), for generality and in attaching it to the attribute rather than to the essence. So the meaning is that He knows the people who hold this attribute and are firmly established in it, from among them and from among others, and so He will recompense them for their wrongdoing, and they know this. The greatest confirmer is God, and who is more truthful than God in speech? In this regard, they were never fought except that they retreated into their fortresses and villages, as has passed in Surah al-Hashr (59). This indicates that they are more eager for the life of this world than those who associated partners with God, as has passed in Surah al-Baqarah (2), for they know that they will go to the Fire, while the Arabs assumed that they would not be resurrected, so they did not fear [anything] after death, and they were brave, advancing upon death, as ʿAntarah ibn Shaddad al-ʿAbsi said:

Fate has begun to frighten me, as if I
had become remote from the reach of deaths.

So I answered her: death is a watering place,
and I must be given drink from that watering place.

So spare me, may your life be spared, and do not be the father of a loss; know
that I am a man who will die if I am not killed.

When al-Biqa'i's commentary (Nazm al-Durar) reaches this point, it reads as follows.

Since their not wishing for death was a sign (ʿalam) among the signs of his prophethood (ﷺ), because it agreed with what he had reported, and since that behaviour was the act of one who believes that wishing for death brings it forward from its term and refraining from it delays it, they came to stand between denial of what they had in their possession and utter stupidity. He (ﷺ) was commanded to alert them to their stupidity as a rebuke to them, so He said: ﴿Say﴾. He emphasised it to inform them that their action entails the denial of death, which none of them denies (p-61), so He said: ﴿Indeed, death﴾. He increased the reproach and rebuke with His words: ﴿from which you flee﴾, meaning by refraining from wishing, which is the easiest thing to do, even though it leads you to deny the one whom you strive hard to deny. He emphasised its occurrence for them because their conduct is the conduct of one who denies it. He linked it with the particle fa' (then/so), making their fleeing like the cause of it, for cowardice is among the causes of death, along with the shame it earns, as he said: "Indeed the coward's death is from above him" (meaning it overpowers him as the high overpowers the low). So He said: ﴿for indeed it will meet you﴾, meaning it will overtake you in every direction you take, outwardly or inwardly.

Since detention in the barzakh (the intermediate state) is a matter that is terrifying, though it is unavoidable, He alerted to it and to its length by the particle of delay, so He said: ﴿Then you will be returned﴾. By using the passive form He alerted to His dominance over it, glorified be He, and to their humiliation, and that it is, for Him, in the utmost ease: ﴿to the Knower of the unseen﴾, which is everything hidden from the servants; so He informs you of your deeds with knowledge. Since some philosophers acknowledged His knowledge of universals but denied His knowledge of particulars, He said: ﴿and the visible﴾, which is everything that manifests and becomes individuated, even if to only one of the creatures, before its existence and after its existence. Since questioning about deeds is dreadful and terrifying, He said, as a consequence of the return: ﴿So He will inform you﴾, meaning He will tell you with a great, thorough and complete informing ﴿of what you used to﴾ (p-62) ﴿do﴾, meaning of every part of it, of what has come forth into the outside and of what was in your natures, even if you had forgotten it, so that He may recompense you for it.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 62, verse 9:

When Allah, glory be to Him, condemned the discrepancy between speech and action, and depicted its practitioner in the form of the donkey in the earlier description, and warned against it by means of what prepares the intellect to answer by persisting in obedience, after He had shown that all created beings acknowledge the comprehensiveness of His dominion through the glorification they offer by the tongue of their states, and their standing in fulfilling His wishes with utmost compliance, the intelligent person was worthy of hastening to the utmost glorification by the tongue of speech. He concluded with a warning about the report on the great day of gathering, concerning all deeds. He said, by way of inference from what preceded of encouragement and warning, calling them, so that they might be the friends of Allah, to the purification mentioned, which is the fruit of the message, with what amounts to turning wholly toward Allah and turning wholly away from this world, so that the accountable person may combine adorning himself with virtues and emptying himself of base things. He singled out, from among the virtues, the greatest glorification that the intelligent person performs in the days of the week, which is hastening to the great gathering on the day of Friday (al-Jumu'ah), which corresponds to the gathering in answer to the caller on the greatest day of gathering. Then comes the greatest turning toward Allah by performing [the prayer of] al-Jumu'ah, which is the secret of the day that [the Jews] neglected, and they exchanged it for what was the cause of their torment, with a punishment with which none of the worlds was punished. Just as He made the outcome of (p-63) the previous surah the call to guidance toward faith and struggle, which brings security: ﴿O you who believe﴾, meaning those who affirmed with their tongues the faith, and He urged them with the particle of distance, which indicates their need for purification, to hasten to turning toward what follows from that of commands: ﴿when the call is made﴾, meaning from whatever caller there may be among those who make the call, ﴿for the prayer﴾, meaning for the sake of attending it, and attending Him, when the imam sits upon the minbar (pulpit) for the khutbah (sermon).

Since the response is obligatory and it suffices for its obligation that the call be made at the time known for the call, and it is not required that the call extend over the entire day, He brought the preposition and said: ﴿from the day of Friday (al-Jumu'ah)﴾, meaning the day that was presented to those before us, and they refused it, so they were like the donkey carrying books, and Allah reserved it for us and enabled us to accept it, so they became followers of us, though they preceded us in time. It was named thus because gathering for prayer is obligatory on it. The form fu'lah with sukun, and it may be pronounced with a damma, is a noun of the object, like al-Duhkah for the one laughed at. If its mim is pronounced with a fatha, it carries the meaning of the time of gathering, like al-Dahkah for one who laughs much. Among the reasons for its being so called is that on it the creation of Adam, upon him be prayer and peace, was gathered, so that through his creation all creation was gathered. It reminds of the day of resurrection and the gathering, on which the reporting of deeds takes place, and on which majesty and beauty become manifest, clearly and completely. ﴿On the day when the caller calls from a near place﴾ [Qaf: 41], and on it the Hour will be established. Malik narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), (p-64) that he said: "The best day on which the sun rises is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was brought down, on it he died, on it he was forgiven, and on it the Hour will be established. There is no creature but that it is attentive on Friday from the time it rises until the sun rises, fearful of the Hour, except the jinn and mankind. On it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant who is praying and asks Allah for something will fail to be given it." At the end of the hadith, Abdullah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is the last hour of the day of Friday." The beginning of the prayer is with what is more general than performing it and waiting for it, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever sits in a sitting waiting for the prayer, he is in prayer until he prays it." At the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), the call was made at the door of the mosque when he (ﷺ) ascended the minbar. When he descended after the khutbah, the prayer was established. It was likewise in the time of Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. When Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, came, the people increased, the dwellings spread apart, and aspirations diminished, so he added another caller at his house, which is called al-Zawra'. When he sat on the minbar, the caller called the second adhan, which was the adhan of the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). When he descended from the minbar, the prayer was established. No one censured Uthman for adding the first adhan, since they knew that it is from the Sunnah, by what the Prophet (ﷺ) entrusted to him when he said: "Adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided Caliphs (al-Khulafa' al-Rashidun) after me."

(p-65) Since the intended meaning is the obligation of the matter, decisively, without hesitation, with the severing of every attachment and without turning to anything other than what the Lawgiver has excused, He expressed it by striving (al-sa'y), which is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan that it is striving by intention, not by the foot. So He said: ﴿then hasten﴾, meaning, so that you may be the friends of Allah, and do not be negligent in that, lest you become His enemies like the Jews, ﴿to the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning the khutbah and the prayer, which remind of the great King, whoever is cut off from His service is ruined. This is the intended meaning of striving; it is not literal running, rather that is forbidden, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the prayer is established, do not come to it running, but come to it with tranquility. What you catch, pray, and what you miss, complete."

Since He commanded hastening toward the trade of the Hereafter, and since seeking profits, because they are present, is the greatest obstacle to matters of the Hereafter, [because they are] its ultimate goal, and since selling is the most prominent of that, as its gain is definite, and because it is what the people of the markets most occupy themselves with, due to the abundance of those arriving in the cities on Friday from the settlements, and their gathering for trade when the day rises high, He said, forbidding the trade of this world and everything that hinders from the Friday prayer, expressing it through it because it is the greatest of them: ﴿and leave off trade﴾, meaning abandon it, even in its worst, most base, and most contemptible states. [This indicates] the prohibition of other than it by way of a fortiori. The time of prohibition is from the zenith (zawal) until the completion of the prayer. If one violates this and sells, the contract is valid along with his disobedience, for the prohibition is not (p-66) in its essence, nor in what is part of it, nor in what is external and necessarily connected to it, but rather for a matter concomitant by way of coincidence, namely the heedlessness from the obligation in which he is. It is like praying in a usurped house, a usurped garment, or performing ablution with usurped water.

Since He commanded what is hard upon souls, expressing it by a sick act in wording and meaning, He encouraged it by His saying: ﴿That﴾, meaning the matter of high rank, the act of striving and leaving off preoccupation with this world, ﴿is better for you﴾, because He who commanded you has all the command, and He wishes to purify you in your religions, your bodies, and your wealth, and in His hand is your happiness and your misery. He urged toward this and increased the exhortation to it by His saying: ﴿if you know﴾, meaning, with what is for you like an innate disposition, ﴿know﴾, meaning, that knowledge is renewed for you on some day of the days, so you see that as good, [and when you know it as good, you turn toward it, and that becomes good for you]. The Friday prayer is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) upon everyone who combines puberty, reason, freedom, maleness, and residence, provided he has no excuse of what the jurists have mentioned. He expressed it in this manner only to indicate that an intelligent person cannot allow himself to abandon what he knows to be the highest form of good. Whoever is not obligated to attend the Friday prayer, if he attends and prays with the imam, the obligation of the noon prayer falls from him, but he does not complete the number for the Friday prayer, except for one who has an excuse; for if such a person attends, the number is completed by him.

(p-67)

When he urged the prayer and guided people that its time is not suitable for seeking anything other than it, and that whoever seeks worldly gain during it, its blessing is destroyed along with whatever sin he has earned, he (Allah) permitted for them between the time of prayer and the time of livelihood what He had forbidden them. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "If you wish, go out; if you wish, sit down." ﴿Then when the prayer is concluded﴾, meaning when it is finished in whatever manner it was performed, ﴿then disperse﴾, meaning spread out and scatter through the land, striving in that, ﴿throughout the land﴾, all of it if you wish, with no restriction upon you and no blame, as a concession from Allah to you. ﴿And seek﴾, meaning intend and exert yourselves, striving diligently in the pursuit of livelihood, ﴿of Allah's bounty﴾, meaning the bounty of the Supreme King, who possesses all perfection, and no one is owed anything by Him through buying, selling, or other matters of the interests of religion and worldly life which you had been forbidden to pursue during the prayer.

Since the striving for sustenance is distracting from the remembrance (of Allah), He made clear that the greatest of all striving in livelihood is that remembrance, and that whoever neglects it will not achieve any goal, however much he schemes with every kind of stratagem and otherwise. So He said: ﴿And remember Allah often﴾, meaning the One in whose hand is every thing, and nothing belongs to anyone else. There is no concession at all for abandoning His remembrance. Since the servant is required to worship in every state, and he is naturally disposed to forgetfulness, whenever he slackens in himself, heedlessness takes hold of him, he becomes accustomed to idleness, and he is ruined. He said: ﴿often﴾, meaning in such a way that you never neglect Him at all, neither in your hearts nor with your tongues, even upon entering the lavatory, at the beginning of intercourse, and at the time of ejaculation. He excepted the tongue at the time of being engaged with something impure, such as being in the state of relieving oneself.

Since the aim of a person in all his actions is to attain what he desires, He stated, giving the reason for this command: ﴿so that you may be successful﴾, meaning so that you may be, in the eyes of the observer and the one who watches over you from among your peers who are ignorant of the outcomes, in hope that you will attain all that you seek. For all matters are in the hand of the One whom you remember often, and He knows who deserves success, so He grants it to him, and who acted for show or the like, so He disappoints him. So when you obey His command, you are worthy of receiving what you want, and if you forget Him, you are deserving that He leave you to yourselves, and you will perish.

(p. 69) Since the implied sense, as the wording of the address expresses it, is: "These are Our noble commands, Our great sanctifications, and Our abundant, generous favours. So what is wrong with them? When it is called to them, some of them are slack in turning towards it, and their hearts are inclined toward trade and other worldly matters, devoted to them, striving with all their effort toward them, contrary to their statement that they have submitted to the Lord of the worlds in this act of theirs," He followed this by saying: ﴿And when they see﴾, meaning, after arriving at its (the market's) pleasant place and its spacious, fine-expanded location, and after being occupied with its exalted affair, ﴿a trade﴾, meaning cargo that is a subject of trade. When He mentioned that which is of the nature of sustaining livelihood, He followed it with what is lower than it, which is the least of its concerns, idle pastime, which a person of worth does not incline to and does not give his mind to. So He said: ﴿or a diversion﴾, meaning whatever distracts from every beneficial thing.

Since the mere scattering (infidad) is ugly, because it occurs only as a near-response to a bad state, from *al-fadd* (breaking by dispersing), and *al-fudaad* is what has scattered from the mouth and from the spathe (of the palm), meaning he broke them, how much more so when its cause is ugly. Thus the Exalted said, expressing it by it: ﴿they scattered﴾, meaning they dispersed, scattering out of haste.

Since the occasion of the revelation of the verse was that the people had been struck by hunger and hardship, Dihya al-Kalbi, may Allah have mercy on him, lost a camel carrying provisions. It was their custom that when such (caravans) entered they would do so with drums, musical instruments and shouting. Some of those who scattered were aiming at the caravan, and some were aiming at the diversion that accompanied it, but the one intending trade was the majority. He made the pronoun feminine and said, indicating by it concern for it, because the diversion is caused by it: ﴿towards it﴾. And to show that if the one who intends it is blamed, even though it contains benefit, and a person must necessarily set right his livelihood for the sustaining of his condition, especially when the need at that time was severe, then blame for intending diversion is all the more fitting.

Since this was the state of the sermon, which deserves intense attention and admonition, for turning the soul away from the world and turning it towards the Hereafter, He said: ﴿and they left you﴾, meaning while you were preaching, until you remained with twelve men. Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I was one of them." It indicated the legitimacy of standing by His words: ﴿standing﴾. So the obligatory (form) is two sermons, standing, separated by a sitting. The obligatory elements in both are that one praise Allah the Exalted, send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and exhort towards the fear of Allah the Exalted. These three are obligatory in both sermons together. It is also obligatory that one recite in the first a verse of the Qur'an, and in the second that one supplicate for the believers. So if one omits any one of these five, the sermon is not valid according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him. For the validity of the Friday congregation there are five conditions: the time, which is the time of noon; the number, which is forty; the imam; the sermon; and the place of residence. If any condition is lacking, the noon prayer becomes obligatory. The sermon is not begun until (the people) are complete, and the continuance of this number is a condition until the end of the prayer. If some of them scatter and then return, and nothing of the pillars (of the prayer) has been missed, it remains valid.

Since this was the act of one whose aspiration is low regarding hearing the word of Truth from the Truth, He commanded him ﷺ to admonish them, urging them to return to their state of being fit for address, even if by reproach. He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning to them, encouraging them to return to what they had been upon of seeking good from its source: ﴿What is with Allah﴾, meaning the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, of the immediate benefits in this world, from the inspirations of the hearts and the first appearances of reality, which result from hearing the sermon that commands every good and forbids every evil, that gives benefit in purifying the inward and rectifying the outward, and blessing in all conditions, and of the deferred benefits in the Hereafter, which is of what ﴿is better﴾ than any description. And since he had first placed trade first out of concern for it, he here placed what was its cause, so that each of them would be an object of the prohibition. So He said: ﴿than diversion﴾. And since he began with it because the majority in the state of comfort incline toward it, he said, repeating the preposition for emphasis: ﴿and than trade﴾, meaning even if it is great.

Since one who possesses a thing may not give it easily, and when he gives it, gives only to one he loves, He said: ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning the Possessor of majesty and honour alone, ﴿is the best of providers﴾, because He provides the enjoyment of this world for its lowliness and as provision for the Hereafter, to the righteous and the wicked, the obedient and the disobedient, and He gives whom He wills what cannot be counted nor confined by limit. As for the divine knowledges and the religious acts indicated by the radiance of sincerity, the purity of devotion and the grandeur of following (the Prophet), He does not bestow them except upon the righteous, even if they are the weakest of people and furthest from that. And He does not deprive anyone who turns to what He has legislated, a thing that would benefit him. So do not suppose that wealth lies in buying and trading, but rather it lies in following the command of the One who permitted trade, commanded it, and legislated what is better than it in purification, blessing and growth in the outward and the inward. Ṣāḥib al-Firdaws (Shīrawayh, the compiler of the work *al-Firdaws*) narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever says on Friday, 'O Allah, enrich me with what is lawful from what is unlawful, with Your obedience from Your disobedience, and with Your bounty from others than You,' seventy times, no two Fridays will pass over him before Allah the Exalted enriches him." The origin of the hadith was narrated by Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who said it is ḥasan, on the authority of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him; and there is a corroborating report on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. So turn towards the following of His Messenger ﷺ, adhere to his guidance, and hold fast to his stirrup, and you will attain the good of both abodes with ease. Thus the end of the sūrah, as you see, returns to its beginning, with what belongs to the King regarding provision, granting profits and benefits, especially when He is the Holy One; and the rebuke of those who turned away from the sermon of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which necessarily implies continued turning towards him and enduring presence before him, because he calls them only to what gives them life, of prayer and admonition, which is itself the glorification of Allah and His exalting above imperfection: ﴿He recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2]. Their Lord purifies them and provides for them of His bounty; indeed He is Generous and the Giver of gifts. And Allah knows best what is correct.
